name: OmniRoute
summary: A local gateway that picks which model serves each request and falls back to the next one when a provider runs out of quota. Providers and keys are added in its own dashboard.

steps.title: OmniRoute is running
steps.text: Start it from the Services screen if it is stopped.

steps.title: Set the admin password
steps.text: Open http://localhost:20128 in your browser and set the admin password. You do this yourself; this app never sees it.

steps.title: Connect your providers
steps.text: In the dashboard, connect what you have: your Claude subscription, Codex or OpenAI, OpenRouter, free tiers, anything else you add later. Sign-ins and keys are typed into OmniRoute only.

steps.title: Create the three combos
steps.text: Create three combos named exactly fast, balanced and frontier. In each, put your providers in the order you want them tried: first choice first, then what to use when it is out of quota.

steps.title: Create an API key and save it
steps.text: In the dashboard create one API key. Then in Ubuntu create the file ~/.agent-stack/secrets/OMNIROUTE_API_KEY and paste the key into it yourself.

steps.title: Key file is in place
steps.text: Checks that the file exists. Its contents are never read by this app.

steps.title: Point the router at OmniRoute
steps.text: Backs up the router's settings, switches its fast, balanced and frontier tiers to OmniRoute, tests it live, and puts the old settings back automatically if the test fails. If something is missing it changes nothing and tells you what.

steps.title: Check it is wired
steps.text: Confirms the router now sends those tiers through OmniRoute.
